why: Anyone opening the codebase to make a change first asks where things live. A short map of the main folders saves them from digging through every directory.
question: Where are the files if I want to change something?
questionNote: Once it runs and you want to edit code
who: Required for course examples and backend APIs
whoNote: Recommended whenever there are several folders

parts.heading: One or two important folder levels
parts.text: Put the tree inside a text code block, show only the top one or two levels that matter, and make sure every folder name matches the repository.
parts.emphasis: Do not paste raw tree output with dozens of files or node_modules.

parts.heading: One-line purpose and boundaries
parts.text: Write what belongs in each folder, especially rules that are not obvious from the name—such as "All API calls live here; components do not call fetch directly".

notes.title: Dumps the whole tree
notes.text: Skip node_modules and individual files; show two levels.

notes.title: Folders have no descriptions
notes.text: Add a short phrase beside each folder explaining its role.

notes.title: Folders do not exist
notes.text: Remove leftover template folders so paths match the repo.

lines: ├── docs/images/    Screenshots used in the README
├── api/        Order API calls (no direct fetch)
├── components/ UI components such as menu cards
└── views/      Pages such as order and cart

tip.title: Explain boundaries that are not obvious from the folder name
paragraphs: Writing "components" next to components/ adds nothing new; writing "shared buttons and modals; page-specific ones stay next to their page" actually helps.
AI tools also read this map before adding files—clear boundaries keep them from putting code in the wrong directory.

types.web-app: Show where pages, shared components, state, and API calls each live.
types.course-example: Point out which files students should edit and which folders they can leave alone.
types.portfolio: If you organized the folders around a specific pattern, highlight it here in one line.
types.backend-api: Show where routes, business logic, database models, and migrations are kept.
